item.title: C/C++ Compiler Tokenization: Why 'a+++++b' Fails Lexical Analysis
item.description:
“C/C++ Compiler Tokenization: Why ‘a+++++b’ Fails Lexical Analysis”

When encountering complex operator sequences in C or C++, such as a+++++b or intricate printf statements like printf("%d",a+++++b);, the resulting compilation error—often involving “lvalue required as increment operand”—can be perplexing. What exactly is the compiler doing when it consumes these characters, and why does it select one interpretation over another? The key lies deep within the lexical analysis phase, specifically the Maximal Munch Rule.
